overview: A limit switch detects that something has physically reached a specific position — a 3D printer axis hitting the end of its travel, a door reaching fully open, a CNC machine's carriage at its home position — by having a lever or plunger mechanically triggered at exactly that point. Unlike most sensors in this encyclopedia, it's satisfyingly simple: a mechanical switch with a satisfying positive 'click' and no calibration, drift, or environmental sensitivity to worry about, which is exactly why it's still the standard choice for homing and end-of-travel safety even in otherwise all-electronic designs. Most have three terminals (COM, NO, NC) rather than just two, letting a circuit choose whether the switch should be normally-open or normally-closed for its specific safety logic.
simpleSummary: A switch that gets pressed automatically when something reaches a specific spot, like a printer arm hitting its limit.

specifications.switchType: SPDT (single-pole double-throw) — provides both normally-open and normally-closed contacts
specifications.actuationMethod: Lever, roller lever, or plain plunger depending on variant
specifications.ratedVoltage: Often rated for both low-voltage logic and higher mains-adjacent voltages/currents
specifications.mechanicalLife: Typically rated for hundreds of thousands to millions of actuations

pinMap.name: COM
pinMap.function: Common terminal — connects to either NO or NC depending on actuation state.
pinMap.voltageRange: Logic-level or higher depending on rating
pinMap.currentLimit: Depends on switch rating (often several amps)

pinMap.name: NO
pinMap.function: Normally-open contact — connects to COM only when the switch is actuated (pressed).

pinMap.name: NC
pinMap.function: Normally-closed contact — connects to COM by default, disconnects when the switch is actuated.
pinMap.gotcha: Using NC for safety-critical stops (like an emergency limit) is generally safer than NO, since a broken/disconnected wire then behaves the same as a triggered stop rather than silently failing to trigger at all.

useCases.title: 3D printer/CNC axis homing
useCases.scenario: Detect when an axis reaches its home or end-of-travel position to establish a known reference point.

useCases.title: Door/lid open detection
useCases.scenario: Detect whether a door, lid, or hatch is fully open or closed.

useCases.title: Mechanical safety cutoff
useCases.scenario: Physically stop a motor or mechanism from over-traveling and causing damage.

oftenConfusedWith: Hall effect sensor (contactless, no mechanical wear, but needs a magnet)
oftenUpgradedTo: Optical or magnetic non-contact end-stops for higher precision and no mechanical wear
